tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear Path for Target Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a disk that is not currently the topmost on its peg, relocate every smaller disk that lies above it to other pegs so that the target disk becomes free to move.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever the disk you need to move has one or more smaller disks stacked on top of it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If peg A has [5,4,3,2,1] (1 on top) and you need to move disk 3, first move disks 1 and 2 to other pegs, then move disk 3.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Build Goal Stack in Decreasing Size
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Construct the final tower on the goal peg by placing disks from the largest down to the smallest, ensuring each newly placed disk sits on a larger disk or an empty peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When assembling the final configuration, start with the largest disk that belongs on the goal peg and work downwards.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To achieve [5,4,3,2,1] on peg 2, first ensure 5 is at the bottom, then place 4, then 3, and so on.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Phase Planning (Move‑k‑Disks)
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Solve the sub‑problem of moving k disks by recursively moving the top k‑1 disks to an auxiliary peg, moving the k‑th disk to its destination, then moving the k‑1 disks onto it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to transfer a stack of more than one disk between pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move three disks from A to C using B, first move the top two from A to B, move the third from A to C, then move the two from B to C.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Do Not Prematurely Place Small Disks on Goal
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never move a small disk onto the goal peg before all larger disks that must sit below it have already been placed there.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the goal tower, avoid placing any disk on the goal peg unless every larger disk that belongs below it is already correctly positioned.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If the goal peg should end with [5,4,3,2,1], do not place disk 1 on the goal peg before disk 3 has been placed.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Legal Move Invariant
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Every move must satisfy two conditions: the source disk is the topmost disk on its peg, and the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: For every individual move you generate.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 2 onto a peg whose top disk is 3 is legal; moving it onto a peg whose top is 1 is illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat Existing Goal Disks as Fixed Base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Once a disk is correctly placed on the goal peg and all larger disks beneath it are also correctly placed, treat that stack as immovable and never move any of its disks again.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After a disk has reached its final position in the goal configuration.
tower-of-hanoi.example: When the goal peg already contains [5,4] in the correct order, never move 5 or 4 again.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Exploit the Smallest Disk’s Flexibility
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating size constraints, making it ideal for temporary shuffling while larger disks are being moved.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need a temporary buffer and any peg is available.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Move disk 1 to an empty peg to free a larger disk, then later move it back on top of the rebuilt stack.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Post‑Construction Verification
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the full move list, replay the moves from the initial configuration to confirm that each move is legal and that the final configuration matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the end of the planning phase, before outputting the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Simulate the sequence [[1,2,1], …] and check that the final peg states equal the target.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Generate Moves Recursively with Explicit Disk IDs
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When implementing the recursive Hanoi algorithm, explicitly name the disk being moved in each step, rather than using generic 'move top disk' statements, to avoid ambiguity and ensure correct parsing.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During move generation, especially when the output format requires [disk_id, from_peg, to_peg] triples.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Instead of 'move top from A to B', output [1,0,2] for moving disk 1 from peg 0 to peg 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Move Two Smallest Disks as a Unit
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When a target disk is blocked by exactly two smaller disks, clear the path using a three‑move pattern: move the smallest to an auxiliary peg, move the second smallest to the destination peg, then move the smallest onto the second smallest. This restores the two‑disk stack on the destination and frees the target disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: If the disk you need to move has two smaller disks on top of it and the destination peg is ready to receive the target, apply this three‑move subroutine before moving the target.
tower-of-hanoi.example: From source peg S with top sequence [2,1] and target disk 3 below, perform: 1→A, 2→D, 1→D, then move 3→D.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may focus on moving the desired disk without checking the size of the top disk on the destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always verify that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk before committing to a move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempting to move a disk that is not the topmost on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may overlook that only the top disk can be moved, especially when the target disk is buried under smaller ones.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: First clear any smaller disks above the target using the 'Clear Path for Target Disk' subroutine.

tower-of-hanoi.description: The sequence of moves ends with a configuration that differs from the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop early or misplace disks, often due to premature placement of small disks on the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After generating moves, run a post‑construction verification to ensure the final state matches the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Using the wrong peg numbers (e.g., 1 instead of 0) when listing moves.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Confusion between 0‑based indexing required by the verifier and natural 1‑based counting.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always remember that pegs are indexed 0, 1, 2; double‑check each move's from_peg and to_peg values.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Placing a small disk onto the goal peg before all larger required disks have been positioned beneath it.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may try to finish quickly by dumping small disks onto the goal peg without respecting the final ordering.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Apply the 'Do Not Prematurely Place Small Disks on Goal' rule; only place a disk on the goal peg when all larger disks that belong below it are already fixed.
